Villeray is the central part of the Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension borough: the
Metropolitan autoroute to the north, Parc-Extension beyond parc Jarry and the railway to the
west, Saint-Michel to the east, and Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie across rue Jean-Talon to the
south. This report compares every
francophone public elementary school in it: nine whose building lies inside the quartier as the
city draws it, and one just outside its southern boundary within 300 m, Saint-Arsène, marked †
throughout. For each school it shows the school itself, the kilometre around its building on
the same metrics as a school report, and the three-bedroom homes listed near it this month. It
is the first output of MTL-101's `quartier-report` skill, run as a dry run.

::: {.callout-important}
## Not a ranking

Each zone metric is shown with its decile among the 229 francophone public elementary schools on
the island outside the West Island, marked [d1]{.decile-low} to [d3]{.decile-low} for the lowest
three tenths, [d4]{.decile-mid} to [d7]{.decile-mid} for the middle, and [d8]{.decile-high} to
[d10]{.decile-high} for the top three. A high decile means a high value, nothing more, so the
column header says which way is favourable for a family: ▲ higher is favourable, ▼ lower is
favourable, and columns with no glyph are descriptive. In the ▲ and ▼ columns the most
favourable school is [shaded]{.best}. The report computes no composite score and names no best
school; the IMSE is a socioeconomic index of the pupils enrolled, not a measure of academic
performance.
:::

# The area

The polygon is the city's *quartier sociologique*, 5.67 km² in Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-
Extension. Each pin is a school building; the dashed pin is the edge school; M squares are the
three métro stations inside the quartier, Jarry, De Castelnau and D'Iberville; Jean-Talon
station lies just outside its boundary.

::: {.callout-note}
## Also in the quartier, outside this report's scope

- **École Victor-Doré**, 1350 boulevard Crémazie Est: a CSSDM specialised school with a
  supraregional mandate for pupils aged 4 to 13 with serious motor or organic disabilities;
  most pupils come from other service centres, so it is not a neighbourhood option and is left
  out of the tables.[^vd]
- **Secondary schools**, all CSSDM: Joseph-Charbonneau and Henri-Julien (rue Rousselot),
  Académie De Roberval and Georges-Vanier (rue Jarry Est), Lucien-Pagé (boulevard
  Saint-Laurent). Which of them a given elementary school feeds is not yet in the project's
  data.
- **Centre Sainte-Croix**, adult education, rue Jarry Ouest.
- No anglophone-board or private school has its building inside the polygon.
:::

[^vd]: [École Victor-Doré, école spécialisée](https://victor-dore.cssdm.gouv.qc.ca/ecole/), CSSDM; read through its search-index extract on 2026-10-07 and recorded in the project's program table.

: The schools at a glance: IMSE decile from the MEQ file (socioeconomic, not academic), zone metrics within 1 km of each building with island deciles; † = outside the area but within the margin {#tbl-overview}
:::

The MEQ's IMSE decile (1 = most advantaged, 10 = most disadvantaged; 8 to 10 is the official
*milieu défavorisé*) is built from the enrolled pupils' parents' education and employment, not
from test results, and it can differ from the census figures for the residents of a school's
kilometre. Villeray is the case the project brief uses to make its point: inside one quartier
the deciles run from 3 (Saint-Gérard, Sainte-Cécile) to 10 (Saint-Grégoire-le-Grand), while the
kilometres around those schools differ far less on income in @tbl-people. Program and admission
come from the project's hand-checked table; "unknown" means no page has been checked yet, not a
regular program.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Reading the table

Three schools carry a volet: Saint-Barthélemy's IB primary years programme, selective and
housed at its pavillon Sagard only; Gadbois, an alternative school; and Saint-Gérard's
intensive-English stream for the last two grades. Saint-Arsène, the edge school, runs a
selective athlete programme. The deciles split the quartier in two: the three eastern schools
(Saint-Barthélemy, Saint-Grégoire-le-Grand, Saint-Gabriel-Lalemant) and Saint-Pierre-Apôtre in
the north-west sit in the *milieu défavorisé* band, the schools along avenue De Gaspé and in the
centre of the quartier do not. Every kilometre here is denser and more mobile than the island
median and has fewer children, and only Saint-Grégoire-le-Grand's and Marie-Favery's lie more
than 700 m from a métro.
:::

# The kilometres compared

Every row is the circle of one kilometre around that school's building, a stand-in for the
catchment polygon that exists only in the CSSDM's finder and PDF maps. The *Villeray* row is
computed over the whole polygon, and the island median over all 229 in-scope schools. The
circles overlap heavily: the quartier is 5.67 km² and each circle is 3.1 km².

## Reading the table

Income rises from east to west and north: the two easternmost kilometres sit in the lowest
decile of household income and in high deciles of low income and renters, while the kilometres
around Saint-Gérard and Hélène-Boullé, a few streets west, are in the eighth and ninth deciles
of income. Children are scarce everywhere relative to the island, scarcest around Sainte-Cécile and
Saint-Arsène near Jean-Talon, least so around Saint-Pierre-Apôtre, which also has the most
households with children. Saint-Pierre-Apôtre is the one kilometre where French at home falls
near the island median; everywhere else it is in the top deciles.
:::

## Social deprivation is high across central Montreal

The INSPQ social axis counts people living alone and lone-parent families, which the dense
central boroughs are full of; read it with the households-with-children column of @tbl-people.
The material axis is where Villeray's east–west split shows: more than half the residents
around the two eastern schools live in materially deprived areas, about a fifth or less around
Saint-Gérard, Hélène-Boullé, Sainte-Cécile and Gadbois.
:::

: Safety: SPVM incidents 2023 to 2025 per 1 000 residents per year within 1 km, and SAAQ pedestrian and cyclist victims 2017 to 2021 within 500 m of the school, per year; the area row is computed over the whole polygon, so its point-relative cells are blank {#tbl-safety}

::: {.callout-tip}
## Reading the table

Crime per resident sits between the fourth and eighth deciles across the quartier, lowest around
Gadbois and highest around Saint-Gabriel-Lalemant, Sainte-Cécile and Saint-Arsène, whose circles
take in rue Jean-Talon and its commercial side streets. The walk-to-school
column separates the schools more than crime does: Sainte-Cécile and Saint-Arsène, both within
500 m of rue Jean-Talon, are in the top decile for pedestrian and cyclist victims, while
Saint-Pierre-Apôtre, on a residential street in the north-west, is near the island median.
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
## What these two datasets cannot say

The city states the incident file is not official SPVM statistics; positions are moved to the
nearest intersection and 17% of incidents have no coordinates and are absent from the rates.
The collision extract ends in 2021; its last two years are pandemic years. Both are rates of
reported events, not of risk. The quartier row has no victims-within-500-m figure because that
metric is defined from a school door.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## Reading the tables

Villeray is a plex quartier: about half of the dwellings in every kilometre are in two- to
five-unit buildings, two thirds around Saint-Pierre-Apôtre, and single-family houses are rare
everywhere. The condo share grows towards Jean-Talon and De Gaspé, where the stock is also
oldest. Assessed values follow the income gradient: the two eastern kilometres are at the island
median for a plex, the kilometres around Sainte-Cécile and Saint-Arsène in the ninth decile for
every type. The effective tax rate is identical across the quartier, so the bill differences are
the value differences.
:::

Park space is unevenly spread: the kilometres around Saint-Grégoire-le-Grand (parc
Frédéric-Back and parc Villeray), Hélène-Boullé and Saint-Pierre-Apôtre (parc Jarry) are in the
top deciles, while Saint-Barthélemy's and Saint-Arsène's hold almost none. Six of the ten
buildings are within 400 m of an orange-line station; Gadbois, Saint-Pierre-Apôtre,
Marie-Favery and Saint-Grégoire-le-Grand walk further.

# Which school for which family

Not a ranking: each line points at the table that shows it, and the catchment, not the
circle, decides who may enrol.

- **A volet rather than the neighbourhood school:** Saint-Barthélemy's IB programme (selective,
  pavillon Sagard), Gadbois (alternative), Saint-Gérard's intensive English in grades 5 and 6,
  and Saint-Arsène's athlete stream (@tbl-overview).
- **A park at the door:** Saint-Grégoire-le-Grand, Hélène-Boullé, Saint-Pierre-Apôtre
  (@tbl-parks).
- **The métro at the door:** Sainte-Cécile, Saint-Gabriel-Lalemant, Saint-Gérard, Saint-Arsène,
  Hélène-Boullé and Saint-Barthélemy, all under 400 m (@tbl-parks).
- **The quietest streets for the walk:** Saint-Pierre-Apôtre, then Saint-Gérard (@tbl-safety).
- **The lowest cost of owning:** the two eastern kilometres, Saint-Barthélemy's and
  Saint-Grégoire-le-Grand's, on every housing type (@tbl-cost); several of this month's listings under a
  million dollars were found there (@tbl-for-sale).
- **The most children around:** Saint-Pierre-Apôtre, Saint-Grégoire-le-Grand, Saint-Barthélemy
  (@tbl-people).

## Listings expire

These are the listings found on 7 October 2026, chosen for variety of type rather than as a
sample; each is shown once, under the school whose building is nearest, which is why the
eastern schools carry most of the sale listings and several schools carry none; prices are
asking prices; the section is not refreshed when the post is republished. For a durable
benchmark use the assessed values in @tbl-cost, which reflect the July 2024 market.
:::

# Sources and caveats

- **Area**: Ville de Montréal, *Quartiers sociologiques*, opened on 2026-10-07; Saint-Arsène,
  181 m outside the polygon, included as an edge school; Barthélemy-Vimont, 90 m outside on the
  Parc-Extension side, excluded at the reader's request.
- **School facts**: MEQ school points and *Indices de défavorisation* (school year 2025-2026);
  program and admission from the project's `data/schools_programs.csv` as of 2026-10-07; no
  per-school web research in this report, so renovations and relocations are not covered.
- **Zone tables**: `scripts/zone_stats.py` on open data fetched between 2026-09-18 and
  2026-10-07 (Ville de Montréal, Données Québec, INSPQ, Statistics Canada 2021 Census; métro and
  REM stations from OpenStreetMap contributors); dissemination areas by centroid, 46 to 82 per
  school kilometre and 108 for the quartier; the city's equity index covers all residents of
  every zone; tax bills matched 99.8% to 99.9% of assessment units. Census 2021 is five years
  old; assessed values are from the 2026-2028 roll and reflect the July 2024 market.
- **Listings**: as seen on Centris.ca on 2026-10-07, see the source column of each table.
- **Deciles**: among 229 in-scope schools, from `data/derived/zone_stats_all.parquet`.

# Conclusion

Four readings across the quartier, in the order a parent weighs them. Each states what the
tables show, not a verdict.

**School.** Ten francophone public elementary schools, three with a volet and one selective
athlete stream on the edge; IMSE deciles from 3 to 10 inside one quartier, with the
*milieu défavorisé* band in the east and north-west and the De Gaspé and Saint-Hubert schools
outside it. No school here has a full report yet (@tbl-overview).

**Safety.** Crime per resident runs from the fourth to the eighth decile, with the market and
the Saint-Hubert strip in the higher circles; the walk to school is the sharper line, top
decile at Sainte-Cécile and Saint-Arsène near Jean-Talon, near the island median at
Saint-Pierre-Apôtre (@tbl-safety).

**Livability.** Fewer children than the island everywhere, most around Saint-Pierre-Apôtre;
material deprivation concentrated in the east, social deprivation high across the quartier as
in all of central Montreal; parks top-decile around three schools and almost absent around two;
the métro within 400 m of seven buildings (@tbl-people, @tbl-indices, @tbl-parks).

**Affordability.** A plex quartier with little single-family stock; assessed values at the
island median in the east and in the ninth decile near Jean-Talon, at one effective tax rate;
this month's three-bedroom listings run from a condo at about half a million dollars to plexes
above a million, and rentals from about $1,650 to $2,850 a month (@tbl-stock,
@tbl-cost, @tbl-for-sale, @tbl-for-rent).

Next steps:

1. **Run `/school-report`** on the two or three schools that stand out for the family; this
   report has no per-school research (program pages, renovations, relocations), and seven of the
   ten schools have no program row yet.
2. **Confirm the catchments** for candidate addresses on the CSSDM finder; the kilometres overlap
   heavily and a street can belong to a school two circles away.
3. **What this report does not yet cover**: renovations and relocations, childcare places,
   transit frequency, heat islands, rents by CMHC zone, and which of the quartier's five
   secondary schools each elementary school feeds.

::: {.callout-important}
## Bottom line

Villeray's ten schools sit in kilometres that look alike on density, mobility and language and
differ on income, deprivation and cost along an east–west line, while the schools' own IMSE
deciles span almost the whole scale. The one thing to verify before acting is the catchment of
the candidate address, because in this quartier the nearest school is rarely the only one
within a kilometre.
:::
